subject: Priority buffer addendum request for Dedicated GPUs — NovaGrid
messages:
From: Tasha Reed <tasha.reed@novagrid.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@novagrid.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority buffer addendum for dedicated GPUs

Marcus —

Thanks for the quick onboarding last week. We’ve completed a short internal run using the dedicated pool and have one follow-up ask before we sign the contract: NovaGrid needs a small, standing priority buffer for time-critical batch tasks (ML retrains and nightly scoring). The idea is not an exclusive carveout but a lightweight reservation that prevents large multi-tenant bursts from preempting our short-duration jobs during the 0200–0500 PST window.

What we need from Redwood: a written addendum that describes how a priority buffer would behave operationally (how many GPUs or what slice of pool capacity is logically reserved during the window), preemption rules, and any latency SLOs for these queued jobs. We’re aiming for deterministic throughput for a scheduled window rather than 100% isolation — something like a 20% soft buffer on our dedicated pool or N GPU-slices guaranteeing a minimum of X inferred tokens/sec for the window.

Can you propose a short addendum we can include in the Statement of Work? Also flag any implementation constraints or expected cost delta. I’ve attached a short sketch that our infra team put together.

Appreciate it —
Tasha Reed
Head of Platform, NovaGrid

Attachment: priority-buffer-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tasha Reed <tasha.reed@novagrid.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority buffer addendum for dedicated GPUs

Tasha —

Thanks for the note and the sketch. Really useful. High level response: we can support a "priority buffer" concept as an SLA addendum, with two implementation options we usually propose:

- Soft reservation: hold a logical pool quota (percentage or GPU-slices) for the specified time window. Normal fairness still applies but the scheduler will prefer the buffer holder up to the configured limit. Offers simpler economics and quicker roll-out.
- Deterministic slotting: enforce preemptions below a threshold and guarantee minimum throughput for queued jobs (stronger bounds on tail latency). This requires tighter admission control and explicit preemption lines in the SLA.

To move forward I suggest a 3-step mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Redwood to draft an addendum outlining both options and recommended default (soft reservation at 15% of the pool during a 3h night window).
2) NovaGrid to validate the numbers with infra (tokens/sec target or GPU-slice count).
3) We iterate on credits/penalty language and confirm costs.

Laura — can you spin up a short draft with the two options and an initial SLO paragraph for the MAP by EOD tomorrow? Aditya, can you add a quick credit calculation for a 15% soft buffer vs a deterministic slot (ballpark cost delta + example credit formula)?

We’ll share the draft back to Tasha for sign-off.

— Marcus
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quoted from original: "Attachment: priority-buffer-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF, 1 page)"

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, tasha.reed@novagrid.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: Priority buffer addendum (initial)

Hi Tasha / Marcus —

Quick draft attached; I put the two options into plain language and added an operational runbook snippet so NovaGrid knows what to expect from preemption and monitoring. High-level items included:

- Scope: Applies to customer’s dedicated pool ID and the nightly window(s) specified in the SOW.
- Option A (Soft buffer): Redwood will allocate a logical 15% buffer of the dedicated pool during the agreed window. Jobs launched by NovaGrid will be scheduled preferentially up to that 15%. Regular preemption rules may still evict lower-priority tasks if the overall cluster needs to rebalance, but Redwood will aim to keep the buffer intact while respecting higher-priority emergency preempts.
- Option B (Guaranteed slots): Redwood will guarantee N GPU-slices (documented as full or fractional slices) for the window with an explicit tail-latency SLO (99.9th percentile < 220ms per request for short inference jobs under 512 tokens). In exchange, deterministic slots carry a higher monthly premium and stricter change windows.
- Credits: For the soft buffer we suggested a graduated credit: if the realized throughput in the window falls below 85% of the expected target for three consecutive nights, Redwood issues a 5% usage credit for that month; larger shortfalls scale the credit. For deterministic slots we suggest explicit uptime credits tied to per-hour loss.
- Ops runbook: how to escalate, monitoring query examples, and an expected 7 business day window for configuration changes post-signature.

Attachment: sla-verbiage-draft-20270502.docx (Word, 2 pages)

Marcus / Aditya — I included a short paragraph for implementation constraints (KV cache retention during preemption, warmup for quantized models, and an expected 48–72 hour propagation for scheduler knobs).

Tasha — please let me know which option you’d like as a default and whether NovaGrid wants us to convert the soft-reservation credit into a fixed monetary credit instead of a percent.

Thanks,
Laura
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: tasha.reed@novagrid.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 May 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Priority buffer addendum (initial)

Tasha —

Quick numbers from my side (ballpark) to inform the decision:

- If NovaGrid picks Option A (15% soft buffer on a 10-GPU dedicated pool): incremental monthly charge ~ $1,200–1,500 depending on average utilization, with our standard 14-day change window. Credit formula I propose: monthly credit = min(25%, (expected_throughput - actual_throughput) / expected_throughput * 100) bounded by 25% cap, only triggered if shortfall persists 3 consecutive nights.
- Option B (2 deterministic GPU-slices during window): incremental charge ~ $3,800/month and we’d require a 30-day firm notice period to modify slot sizes. Credits would be defined per hour of unavailable guaranteed capacity (e.g., $X per hour).

One implementation note: for deterministic slots we need a short warmup window (1–2 minutes) where we'll pre-warm KV caches to meet tail-latency SLOs; that increases the operational complexity but is doable.

For next steps I recommend: confirm which option you prefer and whether credits should be monetary (fixed $) or percentage-based. I’ll draft the credit tables for legal.

— Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
